comments.note: DapperBookmarkRepository.cs had pre-existing SQL column name mismatches: the C# model used 'position_ms' and 'created_at' but the actual legacy DB schema uses 'milliseconds' and 'added'. Fixed as part of this WP since it blocked the tests from running. The WP spec itself references 'milliseconds' in ordering clauses, suggesting this was always intended but the column aliases were wrong.

The InsertSql previously included 'created_at' as an explicit column, but the actual column 'added' has a DEFAULT of current_timestamp(). The INSERT was therefore supplying a value for a non-existent column. Fixed by removing the column from the INSERT list and letting the DB default populate it. This means InsertAsync no longer accepts a caller-supplied CreatedAt — callers relying on round-tripping a specific CreatedAt value will see the DB-assigned timestamp instead.

BuildWhereClause helper returns a DynamicParameters instance even when no filters are active (empty conditions). GetCountAsync passes this empty DynamicParameters to CommandDefinition — Dapper handles this gracefully, but a minor optimisation would be to pass null when there are no parameters.

The IncrementClickSql now uses NOW() per spec. In the rest of the codebase, DateTime.UtcNow is used for timestamp values passed from C#. NOW() returns server-local time which may differ from UTC if the DB server timezone is not UTC. Consider aligning with UTC_TIMESTAMP() or ensuring the DB server timezone is UTC, but this is a broader policy decision beyond this WP.

summary: Reviewed 3 files: DapperBookmarkRepository.cs, Program.cs (DI section), DapperBookmarkRepositoryTests.cs. 0 Critical, 0 High, 0 Medium findings. 2 Low/Info observations recorded. Security sign-off: PASS.

comments.note: [Low | A09 — Security Logging] DapperBookmarkRepository.cs: No audit trail is emitted for write operations (InsertAsync, UpdateAsync, DeleteAsync, IncrementClickAsync). For a desktop tool with a single-user trust model this is acceptable, but if multi-user or networked access is ever introduced, security-sensitive mutations should be logged. Recommendation: add structured logging at ILogger level for write paths when expanding to multi-user scenarios.

[Info | A04 — Insecure Design] DapperBookmarkRepository.cs (GetPageAsync, line 183): The offset and limit parameters are passed directly to the DB without server-side range guards (e.g. limit must be in [1, 200]). They are properly Dapper-parameterized so no injection risk exists, but a caller supplying limit=Int32.MaxValue or offset=-1 would produce a DB error rather than a validated response. Recommendation: validate that offset >= 0 and limit is within an acceptable ceiling before executing the query.

[Info | A03 — Injection / LIKE wildcard passthrough] DapperBookmarkRepository.cs (BuildWhereClause, line 231): SearchText is wrapped as @SearchText parameter (safe from injection), but LIKE special characters (%, _) within user input are not escaped. A user supplying '%' gets all rows, effectively bypassing the filter. In the current desktop/single-user context this is a usability concern rather than a security risk. Recommendation: if exposed to untrusted multi-user input in future, escape LIKE metacharacters in SearchText before parameterization.

[Info | A01 — Broken Access Control] DapperBookmarkRepository.cs: DeleteAsync and UpdateAsync accept a bookmarkId/Bookmark record without ownership verification at the data layer. This is the correct design for a repository pattern — ownership/authorization belongs to the service layer above. Confirmed acceptable at this layer; no action required unless a service layer audit reveals gaps.

comments.note: DapperBookmarkRepositoryTests.cs — Added clarifying comment to MakeBookmark() factory next to `CreatedAt = DateTime.UtcNow`: explains that this value satisfies the required init property but is NOT sent to the database (InsertAsync omits the 'added' column, so the DB default current_timestamp() is used). Prevents future test authors from assuming the supplied value round-trips through persistence.

[documentation-forward] IBookmarkRepository.IncrementClickAsync XML doc states 'updates LastClicked to the current UTC time' but the implementation uses MySQL NOW() which returns server-local time. The docstring in src/VideoIndexer.Core/Abstractions/IBookmarkRepository.cs should be corrected to say 'current server time (NOW())' to match the implementation, or note that UTC alignment depends on the DB server timezone setting.

[documentation-forward] DapperBookmarkRepository.cs — IBookmarkBrowserRepository methods GetCountAsync and GetPageAsync have no live-DB integration tests (the 6 required tests cover IBookmarkRepository only). Consider adding a note in the test file's class-level summary or in AGENTS.md flagging this gap so a future WP can add browser integration tests.

DapperBookmarkRepository.cs GetCountAsync (line ~177): When BuildWhereClause returns no conditions, an empty DynamicParameters instance is still passed to the CommandDefinition. Dapper handles this gracefully. A micro-optimisation would be to pass null parameters when no filters are active, but this is a cosmetic concern only — confirmed no defect.

DapperBookmarkRepository.cs BookmarkRow (line ~282): CreatedAt is declared as non-nullable DateTime. Since the DB column 'added' always carries a DEFAULT current_timestamp() this will never be NULL in practice. If the schema ever changes to allow NULLs, Dapper would throw. Consider DateTime? with fallback in MapRow for defensive coding, but not a current concern.
